title: indigo_agent_scheduler: accept additional agent instances such as 'Imager Agent #2' in the agent configuration
description:
Found 2026-11-26 after closing b7873f3d (commit 33d9b31f2). Agents built on indigo_filter.c support additional instances named "%s #%d" (indigo_filter.c:335), e.g. 'Imager Agent #2' or, remotely, 'Imager Agent #2 @ host'; the Imager, Guider and Mount agents expose ADDITIONAL_INSTANCES. The scheduler's name_has_prefix() (indigo_agent_scheduler.c:717) accepts only the base name alone or followed by ' @ ', so role_matches() rejects such names: typing 'Imager Agent #2' into AGENT_SCHEDULER_AGENTS is refused as not a valid agent name, and the AGENT_SCHEDULER_*_AGENT_LIST selectors do not list #N instances. The scheduler therefore cannot be configured to use a second imager, mount or guider agent. Sequencer.js is not affected (it accepts any name; its ' @ host' handling works with #N).

Fix: name_has_prefix() also accepts the base name followed by ' #<digits>', optionally followed by ' @ host' (reject other suffixes). Check every user of the role matching (validation, selector lists, solver prefixes, Scripting Agent suffix stripping/mapping) handles '#N' names. Bump DRIVER_VERSION. Tests in indigo_test/integration/test_agent_scheduler.c: typed 'Imager Agent #2' accepted and used; a '#2' stand-in listed in the selector; 'Mount Agent #2 @ host' accepted; invalid suffixes such as 'Imager Agent #x' or 'Imager Agentx' still rejected. Update the naming rule in indigo_docs/INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md and indigo_drivers/agent_scheduler/doc/SCHEDULER.md (and PROPERTIES.md if it states the rule).

outcome.summary:
Reviewed master...HEAD (5 files).
Parsing: name_has_prefix() accepts the base name, then optionally ' #' followed by one or more digits, then the end of the name or ' @ '. Rejected as intended: 'Imager Agent #x', '#', '#2x', 'Imager Agent#2' and 'Imager Agentx'. No numeric conversion is done, so there is nothing to overflow. isdigit() gets an unsigned char cast and ctype.h is already included.
Edge cases: 'Imager Agent #02' is accepted; filter agents never zero-pad (indigo_filter.c:335 uses %d), so this is harmless. 'Imager Agent #2 @ ' with an empty host is accepted, the same as the pre-existing 'Imager Agent @ '; not a new defect.
Users of the name rule: role_matches() is used by both the validation and add_present_agent(), so the selectors list #N instances. Solver prefixes go through the same function. host_suffix() and scripting_view() look for ' @ ', so 'Imager Agent #2 @ obs2' becomes 'Imager Agent #2' as the Scripting Agent knows it. The suffix mapping in agent_busy_bit() keeps '#N'. Sequencer.js's guider check startsWith('Guider Agent') still holds.
The test is not vacuous: the ticket note records that it failed before the fix. It checks the invalid suffixes, 'Mount Agent #2 @ host', the selector listing and selection, the owner IMAGER and the LOCAL event on the renamed imager. I ran the agent-filtered cases (12 run, 12 passed, including additional_agent_instances_are_accepted), then test-clean.
DRIVER_VERSION is bumped to 0x0300002B. The three docs are consistent with the code. Formatting follows the conventions. No findings.
